hook_line: There's a version of you that most people will never meet, the one who replays a conversation from three years ago at two in the morning
why: Sets up the invisible self—distinct from typical burnout, never tracked or seen.

hook_line: You should know that you are measuring the wrong things. We are extremely good at measuring what's visible—output, revenue, churn, sleep hours, steps.
why: Data-driven hook revealing why emotional exhaustion stays unmeasurable and invisible.

hook_line: There is a concept in psychology called cognitive load, the total mental resources you are using at any moment. Your brain doesn't separate a work problem from an emotional one.
why: Explains the mechanism: unresolved emotional loops drain processing power via the Zeigarnik effect.

hook_line: A few years ago, there was a stretch where I was publishing articles, recording videos, building projects, and showing up to client meetings exactly as expected. From the outside nothing looked wrong.
why: Personal story proving that visible productivity masks internal collapse from invisible burdens.

hook_line: That's why on the day something is quietly wrong, you feel foggy, you forget small things, 40 minutes pass at your desk with nothing to show—you're not lazy, you're running something heavy in the background.
why: Practical symptoms people recognize; shows invisible weight leaks into attention and relationships.

hook_line: I remember a conversation with someone close to me who said, 'You're here, but you're not really here anymore.'
why: Vulnerable turning point: what you thought was hidden becomes visible to people who care about you.

hook_line: The work is quieter than you think. It looks like telling one person one true thing about how you are. It looks like admitting to yourself what happened and how it felt.
why: Practical framework (titration, naming) showing that attention—not resolution—stops the background loop.
